transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um... I'm here because... well, lately I've been having these thoughts. I've started catching myself thinking that it would just be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. And sometimes, when I'm driving home from work, I find myself wondering if my family and my students would just be better off without me. It really scares me, honestly, because I don't want to actually act on it, but the thoughts are just... there.
Have you ever experienced a period of feeling this way in the past, perhaps months or years ago, that eventually went away?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days before, like anyone else, but nothing like this. It's never been this heavy, or lasted this long. This is... this is new for me.
Did these feelings start around the time of a specific event or change in your life?

Yeah, actually. It's been going on for about... I'd say a year and seven months now. That was right around the time I took over the STEM assessment redesign at my school. I had to take that on on top of my regular teaching load, and, well, that's really when all this started.
During these past 19 months, have there been any stretches of a few weeks or more where you felt like your old self again, or has this low mood been present almost every day?
No, I don't think there's been any time where I felt like my old self again. It's just been a constant... heaviness, pretty much every single day. I haven't really had a break from it.
Over these past 19 months, have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns, such as difficulty falling asleep or sleeping much more than usual?

Yeah, definitely. It's... well, I can be completely exhausted at night, but I'll still just lie awake in bed. My mind just keeps replaying all the assessment deadlines, or, you know, classroom mistakes I made that day. And then, when I finally do manage to fall asleep, I almost always wake up around 4 a.m., and I never really get back to sleep after that.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your weight since this started 19 months ago?

Yeah, I have. Most school days, I just... I forget to eat, or I end up avoiding it until late in the afternoon. And because of that, over the past year, my clothes have gotten noticeably looser. I'm not trying to lose weight at all, it's just happening.
Do you find that you have very little energy to get through the day, or do you often feel like you are worth less than other people or that you have failed in some way?

Yeah, the lack of energy is... it's very real. By the time I get through a day of teaching and sit through a department meeting, my body just feels so heavy. It gets to the point where even doing something basic, like making dinner or answering a few parent emails, just feels like climbing a steep hill. I just don't have anything left in the tank by the end of the day.
Do you often find yourself feeling like you are worth less than other people, or do you frequently feel an excessive amount of guilt about things you have or haven't done?

Yeah, I do. Um... it's especially bad when things don't go well at work. Like, if a lesson goes badly or even if a student just looks confused, I immediately take it as proof that I’m letting everyone down. I just keep replaying the moment in my head over and over. It just... it makes me feel like I’m a terrible teacher, and honestly, like I'm a terrible mother, too. I just feel guilty about all of it.
During these past 19 months, have there been any activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy, but now find that you have lost all interest in or no longer get any pleasure from?

Yeah, I have. I used to really look forward to playing softball, going to my book club, and working in my garden. I even liked helping out with the robotics club at school. But now... I just don't get any pleasure from them. Most of the time I end up canceling, or if I do show up, I'm just going through the motions. None of it really feels enjoyable anymore.
Do you find that you are often physically restless, like needing to pace around or being unable to sit still, or conversely, that your movements and speech have become noticeably slower to others?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, my body feels really heavy and tired, like I mentioned, but I don't think my actual movements or my speech are noticeably slower. Nobody has pointed anything like that out to me, anyway. And I definitely don't feel restless or have the urge to pace around. Honestly, I usually just want to sit down.
